title: Cohort audit finds unstable performance in efferocytosis-related prognostic scores
summary: A retrospective audit rebuilt an efferocytosis-related head-and-neck-cancer prognostic analysis in 519 primary tumors after detecting non-primary rows in the original cohort. A Cox-LASSO workflow selected a nine-gene sensitivity score, but its exact composition recurred in none of 500 full-pipeline bootstrap samples and repeated nested cross-validation yielded a mean C-index of 0.587. Survival associations persisted in some analyses while external performance was inconsistent, and a fixed cutoff did not transfer. The authors treat both this reconstruction and the historical six-gene score as hypotheses, with overlapping prior cohorts, no demonstrated causal mechanism and no established clinical utility.

evidence.tested: Retrospective prognostic-score audit in TCGA-HNSC primary tumors (n=519), two external cohorts, full-pipeline bootstrap (500 resamples), repeated nested cross-validation, and donor-aware single-cell analyses.
evidence.unknown: No prospective clinical or experimental validation; the nine-gene signature was unstable and a transportable threshold was not established. Public cohorts overlap with earlier work and are not independent sample-level replication.
evidence.ai_role: Cox-LASSO selected a nine-gene sensitivity score, while a locked six-gene score was audited. The model-based analysis is the clinical prognostic result; it does not establish causality or clinical utility.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher PDF: abstract, cohort definitions, Cox-LASSO Methods, bootstrap/nested-CV Results, external evaluation and limitations; publisher-deposited date metadata.
